claims: The Artemis 2 mission is currently targeted to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, according to updated NASA (.gov) and news reports.
The Artemis 2 mission is a 10-day crewed mission.
The Artemis 2 mission will fly around the Moon to test systems for future human exploration.
April 1, 2026, is the primary target launch date for the Artemis 2 mission.
The initial launch window for the Artemis 2 mission opens on April 1 at approximately 6:24 p.m. ET.
The Artemis 2 mission will take four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon and back.
The Artemis 2 mission marks the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
As of late March 2026, the SLS rocket and Orion capsule have returned to the launch pad, according to Space.com.
Other potential launch windows in early April 2026 include April 2nd through April 6th, notes Florida Today.
